newsitem.title: NORWAY: UBN profit hit by tight margins, costs.
newsitem.headline: UBN profit hit by tight margins, costs.

text.p: Union Bank of Norway (UBN), the country's largest savings bank, said on Thursday tight interest margins and higher costs trimmed nine-month pre-tax profits by four percent to 1.06 billion crowns ($166.2 million) from a year earlier.
"Taking into account that the year has been characterised by tough competition in the market, this result was very good," said group director Tore Knudsen in a statement.
The profit after tax was 755 million crowns, corresponding to a 17.2 percent return on equity and roughly meeting market expectations. The corresponding year-ago figure was 836.
UBN, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, said it had increased lending by 14 percent and deposits by five percent over the last 12 months, mainly in the corporate market.
It said the sharp fall in the interest margin over the last two years was now levelling out. Throughout the second and third quarters, the margin was stable at 3.1 percent, it said.
Net interest income fell to 1.88 billion crowns from 2.09 billion but it was offset by total other income rising to 1.13 billion from 947 million crowns, including income from real estate business.
Total operating expenses, however, increased by more than six percent to 2.04 billion crowns.
"The main reasons for this increase in costs were volume growth, the general rise in salary levels and the costs related to the further improvement of the bank's quality of operations," UBN said.
Operating result before losses were 964 million crowns versus 1.11 billion in the corresponding period last year.
